rhn_oldcollier.text: Forty-one years at the coal face and I still can't walk past a pit head without my knees telling me about it.
The Rhondda Heritage Park is the old Lewis Merthyr colliery. They've kept the winding gear and the lamp room, and old boys like me show people round. I'm the exhibit, really.
We used to sing on the way home. You'd come up out of the dark into the evening and a hundred men would have a hymn going by the first corner.

rhn_washday.text: Monday is washday, cariad, always was. The whole row's out with the sheets and all the gossip goes along the line faster than the wind.
My mam had a rule. Washing out on Monday, Welsh cakes on the bakestone Tuesday, and the coalman paid on Friday. If the coalman was late, the whole week fell over.
Miners used to get coal for the fire as part of the job, tipped outside the front door. They call it concessionary coal. Nobody conceded anything, mind. They dug it.

rhn_kid.text: I got a Welsh cake and a Cobblet in the same day. The Cobblet knocked on my school bag. It wanted the Welsh cake.
Grandad says the coblynau helped miners find coal. I think they mostly help themselves to lunch.

rhn_walker.text: There's a footpath all the way up the ridge above the top terrace. You can see six valleys from the cairn on a clear day.
On a clear day. In the Rhondda that's a theory more than a forecast.
